staticText: Local-first English–Hausa phrasebook with 131 embedded app-local starter records, eleven gender or context notes, and a local address-and-writing guide. The draft has no entry-level source ledger or qualified-speaker sign-off. Optional uncached cloud translation requires explicit, non-persistent page-session consent.
boundaries: The inventory uses Latin-script Boko Hausa, preserves core hooked-letter forms including kuɗi, buƙata, kaɗan, and gyaɗa, and does not provide Ajami transliteration.
Treat kana versus kina, ka versus ki, sunanka versus sunanki, and kewarka versus kewarki as required addressee choices rather than slash-text to read aloud.
Northern Nigerian, Nigerien, Ghanaian, Cameroonian, Chadian, and other regional usage can vary.
Do not claim exhaustive vocabulary, regional coverage, tone or vowel-length annotation, or human-quality translation. Preserve spelling, hooked letters, apostrophes, and punctuation.
Never place raw source or translated text in storage, URLs, analytics, accounts, email, logs, or caches.
